arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: General Verrilli argued the question is whether the opposing sides have standing to challenge the law.
Mr. Jaffer argued plaintiffs have standing due to a substantial risk of acquisition.
Justice Scalia questioned whether the issue belongs to the judiciary under separated powers.
Justice Ginsburg asked if the government could invoke state secrets if standing exists.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests whether plaintiffs can sue over a law that allows foreign surveillance. The core dispute is whether a future, uncertain threat creates legal standing.
